name: Two Knights Defense — Polerio Defense
description: The Polerio Defense (5...Na5) is Black's most popular answer to 4.Ng5 in the Two Knights Defense, chosen in the vast majority of master games. Instead of grabbing the d5-pawn, Black attacks the c4-bishop with tempo, keeps f7 defended, and reaches a solid, flexible position.

lines.name: Polerio Defense — 11.O-O
lines.description: Black meets 4.Ng5 with 5...Na5 (the Polerio Defense), chasing the c4-bishop instead of taking on d5. After 6.Bb5+ c6 7.dxc6 bxc6 8.Be2, Black kicks the knight with 8...h6 and claims space with 9...e4. White prioritizes king safety with 11.O-O while Black castles into a solid position with active pieces.
